question: Under the Biomedical Waste Management Rules, 2016, used needles and syringes from health care facilities should be segregated into which colour-coded bin?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Yellow bags are for anatomical waste, soiled linen, and expired medicines — not sharps.
Red bags contain contaminated recyclable waste such as IV sets, catheters, and gloves.
Correct. BMW Rules 2016 mandate that sharps (needles, blades, scalpels) go into white/translucent puncture-proof containers (Category 6/White container).
Blue bags are used for glassware and metallic implants, not sharps in the 2016 rules.

overallFeedback.feedback: Under BMW Management Rules 2016, sharps (needles, blades, scalpels) must be placed in white/translucent puncture-proof containers. Review the four-colour segregation system.
Well done! BMW Rules 2016 use white/translucent puncture-proof containers for sharps — a critical infection-control detail for all clinical settings.
